title: Quiz Report Card
brief: Build a report card for a finished quiz. You will store the player and the score in the right types, work out a percentage without losing the decimals, chop that percentage down to a whole number with a cast, and make a bool print as a word. Three of this module's traps are waiting in here.

problem.goal: Print a six line report: the player's name, the score, the exact percentage, the percentage as a whole number, the grade letter and whether they passed.
rules: The number of questions must be a constant called TOTAL_QUESTIONS holding 8.
The percentage must be worked out from the variables, not typed in as 87.5, and it must print as 87.5 rather than 87.
The Whole line must come from converting the percentage with static_cast<int>. Note that 87.5 becomes 87, not 88.
Use a char for the grade and a bool for whether they passed. The Passed line must show the word true, not 1.
Keep the score at 7 out of 8 so the expected output matches.

steps: The player name and the score are already declared for you. Read them and notice the type of each.
Add the constant for the number of questions, using `const` and the name TOTAL_QUESTIONS.
Work out the percentage as a `double`. 7 out of 8 must give 87.5, so make sure the division is not whole-number division: get that wrong and you will see 87.
Make a `char` for the grade holding 'A', and a `bool` for passed holding true.
Print the six lines exactly as in the example (the first is written for you). Remember `boolalpha` for the Passed line, then press Check Project.
hints: Press Run before you change anything: one line, `Player: Amara`, appears. Add the Score line next and run again. Growing a program one working line at a time is the whole trick.
A constant looks like any other declaration with `const` in front, for example `const int DAYS_PER_WEEK = 7;`. Yours holds the number of questions.

Think about what `7 * 100 / 8` does with only `int` values: 700 divided by 8 is 87 with a remainder, and the remainder is thrown away. In a similar sum, `goals * 10.0 / games`, the `10.0` makes the whole calculation a `double`. Use the same idea with 100.
Store the percentage, do not just print it: you need it twice, once as it is and once converted. Converting looks like `int wholeMinutes = static_cast<int>(minutes);`, and it chops 87.5 down to 87.
The grade is a single character, so single quotes. Passed is a yes or no, so a `bool` with no quotes at all. If the Passed line shows 1, send `boolalpha` to `cout` before printing it.
The remaining lines all follow the shape of the one written for you. For example, a line with a symbol after the value looks like `cout << "Battery: " << battery << "%" << endl;`
inputHint: This program asks no questions, so leave this empty and just press Run.

tests.name: The player and score lines are right
The percentage kept its decimals (87.5, not 87)
The cast, the grade and the bool (as a word) all print

successMessage: Your report card is complete! 📊 You used five different types in one program, locked a value with const, kept a percentage from being flattened by whole-number division, chopped it down on purpose with a cast, and made a bool speak in words. Next module you stop typing the values in and start asking the person at the keyboard for them.
